newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rate fears seen keeping weak Bunds under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Rate fears seen keeping weak Bunds under pressure.

text.p: Bunds stayed weak in late trade on Friday as the short end of the market came under pressure from heightened fears of a German rate rise after comments from Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum.
September Bund futures were quoted at 102.11 at 1505 GMT, down 28 basis points from Thursday's close, after falling as low as 101.99 earlier in the session.

Dealers predicted the contract would remain wedged between 102.00 and 102.15 until the end of the session. Bunds are likely to stay subdued next week with eyes on the Bundesbank's repo announcement Tuesday and its council meeting Thursday.
Dealers said the market appears to have entered a prolonged period of consolidation.

Gaddum in a newspaper interview published on Friday added to a series of thinly-veiled Bundesbank warnings that rates may be headed higher by saying the the bank was concerned about domestic price pressures and wanted "full scope to act."
He also gave a strong indication that the Bundesbank had departed from its policy of announcing terms of forthcoming weekly repo auctions after each fortnightly council meeting.

After 12 months of fixed repo rates at 3.00 percent, the market's certainty is over since the Bundesbank at its last meeting before its summer break announced the repo terms for just two weeks, leaving markets in the dark about this week's and next week's repos.
Markets are now likely to be kept guessing about possible repo changes each Tuesday when the bank sets its weekly repo auction.
"As regards our decisions we have to operate in a more uncertain environment and therefore want to retain full leeway in our Tuesday allocations," Gaddum told Handelsblatt.

Economists expect the Bundesbank to raise its 3.00 percent repo rate by between 20 and 50 basis points by the end of the year but do not expect a rate move next week, either at Tuesday's repo tender announcement or at the council meeting.

The economists see the Bundesbank's recent warnings of inflationary pressures in Germany are a pretext which has worked neatly to stem the mark's weakening against the dollar by provoking fears of an interest rate rise.
With rate fears in the air, markets will focus on German July M3 data and the Ifo business sentiment index should get close scrutiny.
Economists polled by Reuters on average expect M3 growth to have slowed marginally to 6.3 percent from 6.4 percent in June.
The Ifo institute's business sentiment index for July is expected to rise to 96.6 from 96.00, the fourth monthly rise in a row.
